# ADR-0038: Generated ADR status banners and index

<!-- @generated begin adr-status -->
> **Status:** proposed
<!-- @generated end adr-status -->

<a id="context"></a>
## Context
An ADR's status lives only in its `@doc` block, which is an HTML comment, so GitHub
renders nothing for it ([ADR-0016](0016-docs-as-checked-graph-v2.md)). A superseded ADR,
such as [ADR-0005](0005-plugins-wgsl-and-wasm.md), looks exactly like an accepted one to a
person reading it on GitHub. Nothing on the page says that the decision no longer applies
or which ADR replaced it. There is also no list of ADRs with their status: a reader has to
open each file.

The information is already there. Every ADR declares `status`, `tier` (from ADR-0017 on)
and, when superseded, `superseded_by`. [DOCS › Generated content](../DOCS.md#generated)
already says that derivable content is generated by `xtask`, fenced as
`<!-- @generated begin <name> -->` … `<!-- @generated end <name> -->`, and drift-checked,
and [R-DOC-006](../RULES.md#R-DOC-006) says generated blocks are never edited by hand. No
generator exists yet.

The obstacle is [R-DOC-009](../RULES.md#R-DOC-009): after acceptance, only `status` and
`superseded_by` may change. A visible banner is text in the ADR's body, and it has to
change when the ADR is superseded, which is after it was accepted. The only exception
today is the metadata container, under a repo-wide format ADR. A banner needs a second,
narrow exception. Changing R-DOC-009 and the governance check is a process and governance
decision, so this ADR is Tier 1 ([ADR-0017](0017-adr-decision-tiers.md)).

<a id="decision"></a>
## Decision

**1. A status banner under every ADR's title.**
- Directly under the `# ADR-NNNN: …` line, after one blank line, every ADR carries a
  generated block named `adr-status`: the begin marker, one blockquote line, and the end
  marker, each on its own line, followed by a blank line before the rest of the ADR.
- For a superseded ADR the line reads
  `> **Superseded** by [ADR-NNNN: Title](NNNN-….md). This decision no longer applies.`,
  where the ID, title and file name come from the ADR named in `superseded_by`.
- For every other ADR it reads `> **Status:** accepted` (or `proposed`, or `rejected`).
- `docs/adr/TEMPLATE.md` carries the block with `> **Status:** proposed`, so a new ADR
  starts with it.

**2. A generated ADR index at `docs/adr/README.md`.**
- A tracked doc with `kind = "generated"` and `status = "active"`. GitHub shows it when
  someone opens the `docs/adr/` folder.
- The whole file is generated. Its table sits in an `adr-index` block, with one row per
  ADR in number order: the number (linking the ADR), the title, the status, the tier (a
  dash for ADRs from before tiers), and, for a superseded ADR, a link to its successor.
- It is a generated doc, not an ADR, so it may link to superseded ADRs.

**3. One generator, one drift check.**
- `cargo xtask docs generate` writes both from the `@doc` metadata alone: every ADR's
  banner and the index. Running it twice changes nothing.
- `cargo xtask docs check` (CI check `docs`) regenerates both in memory and fails when
  either differs from what is committed, or when a `superseded_by` doesn't name a tracked
  ADR. The fix it names is `cargo xtask docs generate`.

**4. R-DOC-009 gains a second exception.**
- The `adr-status` block is not ADR content. It may change in an accepted ADR, but only
  through the generator, so it always matches the ADR's metadata.
- Everything else stays as it is: the title line and the Context, Decision and
  Consequences sections stay byte-identical, and the rest of R-DOC-009, including the
  metadata-container exception, is unchanged.
- For the same reason, when a section's `depends_on` names a whole ADR, the ADR's body is
  hashed without its banner, as it already is without its metadata blocks
  ([ADR-0039](0039-hash-ignores-metadata-and-row-dependencies.md);
  [DOCS › Hash-bound verification](../DOCS.md#verification)).
  A status change alone doesn't make the dependents stale; a dependency on a superseded
  ADR is already reported by `docs check`.

**5. The governance check ignores a change confined to the generated block.**
- When `cargo xtask governance` compares an accepted ADR, it first removes, from both
  sides, each `adr-status` block whose inside is exactly one blockquote line. A change
  confined to such a block is not a governance change.
- A block of any other shape is not removed, so a change to it is reported as an edit to
  the ADR's content, as today.
- Why not a declared governance change: the block's text is a pure function of metadata,
  and the required `docs` check fails unless it is exactly the generator's output. The
  metadata it is derived from is already guarded: superseding an accepted ADR edits its
  `status`, which is a governance change, and the successor's title is fixed once the
  successor is accepted. Declaring the block too would add a second label requirement for
  the same edit, and noise on every supersession, without catching anything more.

<a id="consequences"></a>
## Consequences
- A reader on GitHub sees at once whether an ADR applies, and where its replacement is.
  `docs/adr/` gains a browsable list of every decision and its status.
- Superseding an ADR now also means running `cargo xtask docs generate`. Forgetting it
  fails the `docs` check with that instruction.
- A new ADR from the template already has the block. One written without it fails the
  `docs` check until the generator adds it.
- **Rule and doc edits, in the same PR as this ADR:**
  - [R-DOC-009](../RULES.md#R-DOC-009) names the `adr-status` exception.
  - [DOCS › Generated content](../DOCS.md#generated) describes both outputs, the command
    and the drift check; [DOCS › The PR gate](../DOCS.md#gate),
    [DOCS › References](../DOCS.md#references) (generated docs may cite superseded ADRs),
    [DOCS › Hash-bound verification](../DOCS.md#verification),
    [DOCS › Governance](../DOCS.md#governance) and
    [DOCS › Bootstrap status](../DOCS.md#bootstrap) follow, and `CLAUDE.md` names the
    command.
- **Governance tool:** `xtask/src/governance.rs` strips the block before comparing an
  accepted ADR, with a test that a change confined to it is not reported.
- **One-time backfill:** every existing ADR gains its banner, through the generator, and
  `docs/adr/README.md` is generated. For accepted ADRs the backfill changes only the
  generated block. The `governance` check of that PR runs the checker built from `main`,
  which doesn't know the exception yet, so it reports each accepted ADR as edited. That
  PR is a declared governance change anyway, because it edits `xtask/src/docs/**`,
  `xtask/src/governance.rs` and `docs/DOCS.md`.
- `docs/adr/TEMPLATE.md` gains the block.
- Because whole-ADR dependency hashes leave out the banner, the backfill makes no
  section stale.
